office_does: A State Senator serves a four-year term writing and voting on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Republican Sen. Drew MacEwen, the Senate Deputy Republican Leader and a 35th District legislator since 2013, faces Democratic Thurston County Commissioner Carolina Mejia. He runs on spending restraint and tax cuts after voting against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million; she runs on cost of living, rural hospitals and infrastructure, and opposes I-1 and I-638.

candidates.summary: Senate Deputy Republican Leader from Shelton, in the Legislature since 2013, a Navy submarine veteran and investment-firm managing partner running on spending restraint and tax relief.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million, and against the 2025 capital-gains/estate and B&O increases [S6][S7][S8]
Top priorities: rein in spending, end tax hikes, cut the sales tax and cap property taxes [S2]
Voted for the 2024 parents' bill of rights (I-2081) and against its 2025 rewrite, ESHB 1296 [S10][S11]
Endorsed by the Association of Washington Business and 16 other trade and professional groups [S5][S15]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346, ESSB 5813 and ESHB 2081 and yes on I-2111; campaigns to end tax hikes, cut the sales tax and cap property taxes.

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls for reining in spending and 'responsible budgeting'; says government 'should live within its means.'

experience.basis: In the Legislature since 2013, Senate Deputy Republican Leader; runs on his 'bipartisan track record.'

social.basis: Voted against ESSB 5599 and ESHB 1469 (2023 reproductive and gender-affirming care bills); no campaign statements or I-638 position.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for I-2081 and against ESHB 1296, the changes I-1 would repeal; no campaign statement on I-1.

candidates.summary: Thurston County commissioner since 2021 and county Board of Health chair, who came to the U.S. from Honduras at 11, running on lowering costs, rural hospitals and infrastructure.
highlights: Would cut permitting delays for housing while 'protecting local control over what development looks like' [S4]
Helped found the Regional Housing Authority and the countywide Home Fund as commissioner [S5][S1]
Pledges to keep reproductive health care 'safe, legal, and accessible'; listed as opposing I-1 and I-638 [S4][S7]
Wants 'strict guardrails' so data centers do not pass energy costs to ratepayers [S4]

spending.basis: Calls for dedicated road and bridge funding, broadband, water-system investment and full state funding of public education.

housing.basis: Pairs cutting permitting red tape with a record of founding a regional housing authority and a county housing fund.

local-control.basis: Wants local control over development and says growth should be shaped by residents, 'not dictated from the outside.'

safety.basis: Prioritizes victim services and a treatment-centered addiction response alongside first-responder funding and gun-safety laws.

healthcare.basis: Wants to cap prescription drug prices, protect existing coverage and keep rural hospitals open; no single-payer statement.

social.basis: Pledges to keep reproductive care safe, legal and accessible; listed as opposing I-638; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and Stonewall Democrats.

parental-rights.basis: Listed among elected officials opposing I-1; no other statement on notification, records or opt-outs.

tech.basis: Wants strict guardrails on data centers' energy costs and pollution.

experience.basis: County commissioner since 2021 with no legislative tenure, running on 'It's time the messenger changed.'
